result: Cutting the number 42 bus would be a false economy for Leeds. Every day, 3,100 people rely on it. The route links two hospitals, so it carries patients to appointments, staff to shifts, and families to the bedsides of people they love. These journeys can't easily be postponed. A woman travelling to chemotherapy, a porter starting an early shift and a teenager visiting a grandparent on a ward have no convenient alternative if the service disappears. Taxis are costly, parking at both sites is notoriously limited, and many of these riders do not own a car. Some will miss appointments, which means worse health outcomes and more expense for the NHS down the line. If the numbers on the spreadsheet look marginal, the council should improve frequency and reliability. Leeds should keep the 42.
